card.title: Weight
card.body: $\vec{W} = m\vec{g}$ (magnitude $W = mg$, directed vertically **downward** toward Earth's center)
card.says: the **gravitational force** a planet pulls on a mass $m$; unlike mass, weight is a vector force and changes if $g$ changes.
card.from: Newton's second law applied to a freely falling body: when gravity is the only force, $W = \sum F = mg$.
card.useWhen: any object is near Earth's surface (or another planet with known $g$) and you need its gravitational force in newtons.
card.example: A $5\text{ kg}$ backpack with $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$ weighs $W = 5 \times 9.8 = 49\text{ N}$ on Earth; on the Moon ($g = 1.6\text{ m/s}^2$), its mass is still $5\text{ kg}$ but $W = 5 \times 1.6 = 8.0\text{ N}$.
card.analogy: Mass is how many bricks are in a bag; weight is how hard the planet pulls down on that bag.
